nodes.description: MMP21 is expressed at the ciliated left-right organizer (the mouse node and zebrafish Kupffer's vesicle) and is part of a genetic module, with DAND5, PKD1L1 and CIROP, that is retained only in vertebrates whose organizer uses motile cilia. In Mmp21-mutant mice nodal cilia beat normally, so MMP21 acts downstream of ciliary motility, in converting the flow signal into left-right identity, rather than in building or powering the cilium.

nodes.description: Biallelic MMP21 variants abolish or reduce the activity of a secreted zinc-dependent metalloprotease. Truncating alleles remove the catalytic and hemopexin domains, and disease-associated missense substitutions fall in core structural elements of the peptidase domain and in its zinc-binding region. The protein's catalytic activity is inferred from its conserved MMP domain architecture; its physiological substrate at the left-right organizer has not been identified.

nodes.description: One study found that MMP21 knockdown increased Notch signaling in vitro and raised Notch target-gene expression in zebrafish. Notch signaling at the left-right organizer balances motile and immotile cilia, so excess Notch activity was proposed as a candidate contributor to the laterality defect. This link has not been independently replicated, and how a secreted protease would restrain Notch signaling is unknown.
